title: simplify tdd for speed: narrow the tier rubric + collapse the two-commit discipline to a single commit (keep red-run evidence)
description:
Human directive (2026-07-12): make development faster by simplifying tdd, WITHOUT losing the anti-test-laundering signal. Chosen approach: (1) bias tier assignment to the lightest defensible tier, and (2) collapse the tdd two-commit discipline to a single test+impl commit while STILL requiring captured red-run evidence. The red-run evidence — proof the tests failed for the right reason before impl — is the load-bearing signal and is KEPT; only the separate test:/impl commit ceremony is dropped.

This is a policy/docs change across every site that states the current rubric or the two-commit discipline. The parity copies (skills/ vs .claude/skills/, agents/ vs .claude/agents/) must stay byte-identical and all doc-lock/calibration sensors must stay green — that's why this goes through the loop rather than a hand-edit.

DO NOT change the src/ code default: CLAUDE.md's 'Absent verification_tier defaults to tdd (backward-compatible)' stays — a ticket with no tier still defaults to tdd (fail-safe). Only the ORCHESTRATOR'S ASSIGNMENT GUIDANCE and the commit discipline change.

Sites to update (find them all; grep 'two-commit', 'strictly before', 'strictly precedes', 'test: commit', 'verification_tier', 'tier rubric'): CLAUDE.md (Workflow step 1 tier assignment, step 4 tdd, the 'Verification tier rubric' section); skills/orchestrator-routing/SKILL.md + .claude/skills/orchestrator-routing/SKILL.md (the 'Single developer spawn, two-commit discipline' section, the Workflow, the tier rubric); agents/developer.md + .claude/agents/developer.md; agents/reviewer.md + .claude/agents/reviewer.md (what the reviewer verifies for tests-first). Also check for any doc-lock/calibration spec that asserts the OLD text and update it in lockstep.
acceptance_criteria: Tier-assignment guidance (CLAUDE.md Workflow step 1 + 'Verification tier rubric' section, and the orchestrator-routing skill's tier guidance) instructs the orchestrator to assign the LIGHTEST DEFENSIBLE tier: tdd RESERVED for security-sensitive logic, parsing, schema/state-schema changes, and state mutation with real edge-risk; tests-after as the default for behavior provable by running the code with low edge-risk; uat-only for glue/config/docs/prototypes. The src/ absent-tier default stays tdd (backward-compat) and is NOT changed — only the assignment guidance.

The two-commit discipline is replaced by a SINGLE-COMMIT tdd discipline at every site: a tdd ticket writes failing tests, CAPTURES the red-run evidence (tests failing for the right reason BEFORE impl), then implements, and MAY commit test+impl together in one commit. The captured red-run evidence in the hand-off is the tests-first proof; a separate test:-before-impl commit is no longer required (but remains allowed).

The reviewer's tests-first verification is updated everywhere it appears (agents/reviewer.md + parity, the skill, CLAUDE.md): instead of 'the test: commit strictly precedes the impl commit', the reviewer verifies the captured red-run evidence is present AND, when the hand-off looks suspicious, reproduces the red state by reverting/stashing the implementation hunks (not by checking out a prior test-only commit). No site still instructs the reviewer to check commit ordering as the tests-first proof.

No leftover contradictory language remains: a repo-wide grep for 'two-commit', 'strictly precedes', 'strictly before' (in the tdd/test-ordering context) returns only historical/changelog references, not live policy. All parity copies (skills/ vs .claude/skills/, agents/ vs .claude/agents/) are byte-identical — parity sensors green.

Any doc-lock or calibration spec that asserted the retired two-commit text is updated in lockstep so it now asserts the single-commit policy (not deleted to dodge the check — re-pointed). npm run test:all green (parity + doc-lock + calibration surfaces). Docs-only: confirm no dist bundle changed (dist-parity green regardless).

UAT: a read-through of the four canonical sites (CLAUDE.md, orchestrator-routing SKILL.md, developer.md, reviewer.md) confirms they tell a consistent story — narrowed rubric + single-commit tdd + red-run-evidence-as-the-proof + reviewer-reproduces-by-revert — with no internal contradiction.

A missing red-run artifact stays a HIGH. PASS.
Step 4 (AC4 — no leftover live contradiction; parity byte-identical): the only remaining "strictly before" (SKILL.md:320) is explicit retired-framing ("originally also carried a two-commit discipline... retired as of TASK-148"). PASS (spec non-vacuity delegated to the gating review).
Step 6 (AC6 — consistent story): the four sites agree — narrowed rubric + single-commit + red-run-evidence-as-proof + reviewer-reproduces-by-revert, no internal contradiction. PASS.

Overall: PASS (6/6). Remaining "two-commit"/"strictly precedes" hits repo-wide are only in historical audit records (tasks/*.json, state/sessions/*, knowledge/graph) and the explicit retired-framing above.
